comments.text: in southern africa the government under aparthied switched the rules on animal ownership, allowing trophy hunting to be a private venture and system, this switched the economic incentive from land destruction for agriculture in places away from national parks where most photosafari tourism exists, to trophy safari hunting and land reclamation, the economic advantages mean more than just numbers, basically by allowing profit in areas that would not see profit from anything other than agriculture, its easy to justify letting the land be the land, and keeping animal herds growing and healthy, when they discovered that killing young bulls was reducing genetic diversity, they came together and said they should switch to perfering to kill post breeding bulls, and thats what they have been switching too, after all low genetic diversity and low head counts, reduce profits, in botswana the elephant population exploded, they kill hundreds of elephants a year now, because numbers are growing beyond carrying capacity, because the system isnt closed and humans exist, animals cant fully exist in the numbers they used to be and must be managed, this system isnt perfect, none is, but it is a system that has shown promise
